findings.source: Li & Subramani, 2026, How Much Do Circuits Tell Us? Measuring the Consistency and Specificity of Language Model Circuits
findings.finding: Component-level circuits can be highly consistent and causally important while being weakly task-specific because the same components are shared across unrelated task circuits.
findings.impact: A future H7 route may be necessary/sufficient yet still be a generic bottleneck. Matched non-target task/context intervention controls are needed before interpreting route effects as lineage-specific responsibility.

findings.source: Meloux, Maniu, Portet & Peyrard, 2025, Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable?
findings.finding: Multiple circuits, interpretations, algorithms and neural localizations can satisfy the same behavioral or causal-alignment criteria even in small networks.
findings.impact: Stable route IDs do not by themselves establish a unique responsible route. Future H7 contracts should distinguish existential route faithfulness from uniqueness-bearing responsibility and use an equivalence-class formulation when alternatives are equally valid.

findings.source: Martinez-Sanchez, Arranz & Lozano-Duran, Nature Communications 2024, Decomposing causality into its synergistic, unique, and redundant components
findings.finding: SURD decomposes causal influence into unique, redundant and synergistic components and quantifies unaccounted influence as a causality leak.
findings.impact: H7 bypass/overdetermination cases can be reduced more finely than deletion accuracy alone. The decomposition is a stronger-privilege ceiling, not an equal-privilege local mechanism baseline or complete actual-causation solution.
